question.problem:
Consider the function $L:{R}^{2}\to R$ defined by $L(x)=2(Ax-b)^{T}(Ax-b)$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 4 & 0 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What is ${∇}_{x}L(x)$ at $x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]?$
question.worked_solution:
We can solve this problem by applying the chain rule for gradients.

Let $y=Ax-b.$ Then, $L(x)=2{y}^{T}y,$ and

$$
{∇}_{x}L={(\frac{\text{d}L}{\text{d}x})}^{T}={(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{T}\cdot {(\frac{\text{d}L}{\text{d}y})}^{T}.
$$

Now, since 

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(2{y}^{T}y)=4{y}^{T}\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(Ax-b)=A,
$$

we have that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{x}L & ={(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x})}^{T}\cdot {(\frac{\text{d}L}{\text{d}y})}^{T} \\  & ={A}^{T}\cdot 4y.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∇}_{x}L & ={A}^{T}\cdot 4y \\  & =4\cdot {A}^{T}(Ax-b) \\  & =4\cdot {[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 4 & 0 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T}([\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 4 & 0 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =4\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & -1 \\ 2 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 16 & -4 \\ 8 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-68 \\ -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
